featured_reviews.name: Ayyub Kolsawala
featured_reviews.review_text:
My favorite thing to do on a Saturday morning is breakfast. So, we drove off to Chembur for the famous Sainath Kulchas. While they serve a variety of Kulchas, through trial and error I have figured out my favorite one.

Firstly, There are a few things that Sainath does that make their Kulchas perfect, the "barrel shaped" tandoor & the quality of the ingredients.

The Aalu Cheese Kulcha 🔥: Delicious Aalu filling with lots of cheese. Baked until crispy in the tandoor. They finish the kulcha with a dollop of butter & sprinkle some Jeera powder to add more flavour. The melted cheese & aalu filling goes great with the crispy kulcha making it the best one in the house! Try the Paneer Kulcha too.

Chola 👎: All the kulchas are served with Chola & some onion salad. However, the chola is never tasty.

Recently they have also introduced a place where you can sit and enjoy the Kulchas. I prefer the comfort of my car though 😇 (if you can find a spot to park).

Bonus:

After the Kulchas, you should try the sugarcane juice right next to it. You could also try the Lassi at Vig. Oh this place takes cash only, the UPI Scanner doesn't work.

featured_reviews.name: Krishnam Mimani
featured_reviews.review_text: This place is at the entrance of a lane right opposite to Ganesh mandir in chembur camp. Consider this place as street food because there's no seating as such. It can only accommodate 4(sitting) persons at a time in the shop. If you go during the afternoon then prepare to be roasted in the sun while eating. The food is average, nothing too great. This place is specifically for kulcha and the chola is like a side dish. I travelled all the way from kalbadevi after watching a reel by some food blogger and I am disappointed. It's not worth the travel. If you live close by and take the food parcel then it might make sense cause this place is affordable. I ordered a alu pyaaz and paneer cheese kulcha and both tasted pretty regular, nothing that would set these apart from any other restaurant. Kulchas are made in a proper tandoor that's all. The total was 180rs which is reasonable. The chole lacks flavours and it's better to have the kulcha without the chole. I honestly don't understand the hype about this place. Only visit this place if you live in the area, otherwise it's not worth the travel.

featured_reviews.review_text:

featured_reviews.name: Rajat Bajaj
featured_reviews.review_text:
I recently visited Vig Restaurant for an authentic Sindhi breakfast experience, and it turned out to be a delightful culinary morning. Located in the heart of Chembur Camp, this well-known Sindhi eatery truly lives up to its reputation for serving traditional flavours at very reasonable prices.

I ordered the classic Dal Pakwaan, and it was everything one expects from a proper Sindhi breakfast. The pakwaan was beautifully crisp, light yet crunchy, and perfectly fried without being greasy. It paired wonderfully with the flavourful dal, which was well-seasoned and comforting. The serving came with aloo subzi, chutney, pyaaz, and pickle, creating a complete and satisfying platter. Every bite had the right balance of spice, tanginess, and texture.

One of the highlights of the visit was their heart-shaped tikki (pattice). Not only was it visually appealing, but it was also deliciously crisp on the outside and soft inside, packed with flavour. It added a special charm to the breakfast spread.

To complete the meal, I enjoyed a chilled mithi lassi — thick, refreshing, and perfectly sweet. As a Punjabi, I always appreciate a good glass of lassi, and this one truly hit the spot. It complemented the spicy breakfast beautifully and made the experience even more enjoyable.

The service was prompt and courteous, adding warmth to the overall visit. The restaurant maintains a simple, authentic vibe that reflects Sindhi culture and hospitality. It felt homely, welcoming, and genuine.

Overall, Vig Restaurant offers a wonderful taste of traditional Sindhi cuisine in Mumbai. Delicious food, generous portions, reasonable pricing, and pleasant service make it a place worth revisiting for a hearty and satisfying breakfast.

featured_reviews.name: swayambharat
featured_reviews.review_text:
Sweet Blind Spot!
While there are enough places serving the usual popular fare- Punjabi, South Indian and Chinese, its kind of difficult to find good Sindhi food baring a few like Nanumal Bhojraj (OG-masjid bunder), Gurukrupa (sion) and Bhagat Tarachand (OG- Kalbadevi) but thats it!
Vig happily fills that void and how!
Just go there on a Sunday morning and one can see a crowd just for takeaways, as the kitchen churns out piles of puris, parathas, kulchas deftly being packed along with Chole, Dal, Chutney and handed over to this never ending stream of customers.
Been yearning to visit Vig in Chembur for ages, and when we landed there, took parcel of an assortment of Aloo Tikkis, Dal Pakwan and Chole Bhature.
More than me, our friends instantly fell in love and planned a visit soon for a repeat!

Sindh Pani Puri Centre in Chembur is a well-loved destination for street food enthusiasts, particularly for those craving a delightful pani puri experience. Known for its consistent quality and authentic flavors, this spot stands out for its exceptional Dahi Pani Puri, a popular variation of the traditional snack.

The Dahi Pani Puri at Sindh Pani Puri Centre is a refreshing take on the classic dish. Each puri is perfectly crisp and golden, providing the ideal vessel for the delicious fillings. The stuffing is a flavorful blend of mashed potatoes and chickpeas, spiced just right to offer a savory contrast to the sweet and tangy toppings. The puris are generously topped with chilled, creamy yogurt, which is smooth and rich, balancing the flavors beautifully.

The addition of tamarind chutney and a sprinkle of chaat masala elevates the dish, adding a burst of sweet and tangy notes that dance on your taste buds. The freshness of the ingredients is evident, making each bite a delightful experience.

The bustling atmosphere at Sindh Pani Puri Centre adds to its charm, with friendly vendors serving up these delightful treats with speed and a smile. Whether you're a seasoned street food aficionado or trying Dahi Pani Puri for the first time, Sindh Pani Puri Centre offers an authentic taste of Mumbai's vibrant street food culture that is not to be missed.

customer_updates.name: Vivek Athavale
customer_updates.text:
Chembur Camp is an area where Sindhis were given a place to reside after they had to leave Pakistan during the partition. I have been in Mumbai for over 25 years and I still didn't know about it. But then that is true for most big cities. To know every part of the city intimately takes a lot of effort and time. I grew up in Nasik and our school was close to Sindhi colony. But in those days I didn't know or care about different types of cultures and food. So all I knew about Sindhi food was that they liked papads. I don't know if that is true but that is what I was told and I believed it .

Inspired by a few food bloggers I follow on Social Media, Chembur Camp has been on my mind for a few years now. I shortlisted the following outlets for my food tour.
1. Chole Kulcha @ Hardev
2. Lassi @ one of the dairies
3. Mutton @ Gopals
4. Something vegetarian @ VIG
5. Sweets @ Jhamas

I reached the main road in Chembur Camp at around 8pm on a Friday evening. I was expecting the place to be crowded and with a queue. This is true for all places ( good and bad) in Cities these days ! I was a little disappointed to see the size of Hardev Kulcha shop. I wasn't sure I had come to the right place. First impressions are important. I looked around unsure of what to do. Close to it is Sainath Kulcha which was also on my list. I saw a few people at the shop.  I made enquires.  Most ppl were like me. People who had come from other areas only to eat Chembur Camp food. I ordered the basic aloo kulcha. I was a bit apprehensive.  The cooks were young and i didn't see any owner at the shop. Not a good sign. The customers at the shop were wierd.
They were asking for Cheese Kulcha without aloo ! Some wanted Kulcha without Aloo or Onion. Quite irritating if you ask me. Especially asking for a cheese only Kulcha.  Almost disrespectful to the Kulcha.  Luckily the Kulcha and Chole were good. Freshly made in the Tandoor. Served along with tangy onion raita. First food item done :).
Next stop was VIG. I was not sure what to eat here. I saw good looking Samosas, Chole and Kulchas which looked a bit different. And then I saw Dal Pakwaan and decided to order it. It was awesome.  Now I had no reference point. It's an interesting dish. A bit oily. But nice. A family run shop. And i have learnt that family run shops normally have great food.
Next on my list was Gopal. Gopal is a meat lovers paradise. I eat Chicken and Mutton but I am not a hard core non-vegetarian. Here the buyers seemed like regulars. Men and Women. Great sign.  They have a restaurant of sorts close by. But this is primarily a take away place. Ideally you should go here in a group. While they have good mutton. They also have a lot of chicken and fish items. I ordered the basic mutton masala which they serve with this special tandoor pav. The mutton was nice. I am not sure it was the best. But it was well cooked and not very oily or spicy. It was a new taste for me. I liked it.  I know I need to make at least one more trip to Gopals to taste their other stuff.  If non veg is your focus then your first and last stop should be this :) . From the outside it looks like just another shop selling Tandoori Chicken and other similar stuff.  But it's not. You will need some help in deciding what to order . You might not get that help at the Delivery Counter and especially during peak hours . But you can't go wrong with your order here. Everything is fresh, fast moving and tasty.
I had the basic but very popular Mutton Masala along with their unique Tandoori Pav. They serve all their dishes with the typical green chutney and chopped onions.
I wish I had the appetite for at least a Kebab or Tandoori Chicken but I didn't.

After that quick meal I went looking for desert. I was going to have Lassi at one of the dairies they have here like Sindh Punjab (it is very popular) but a local recommended to try the Lassi at VIG. And it didn't disappoint. They serve Lassi with fresh cream and it was a great, if a bit too heavy way. That was the end my Chembur Camp food tour.

Had an amazing dining experience at Wok Hei, and it truly exceeded expectations. The ambiance is warm, vibrant, and perfect for enjoying authentic Chinese cuisine. From the very beginning, everything felt well-organized and welcoming.
We started with the Chef’s Crab Soup, which was rich, flavorful, and incredibly comforting. The balance of spices and the generous crab content made it stand out, setting a great tone for the meal. It was easily one of the highlights of our visit.
For the main course, we ordered the Chicken Chinese Sizzlers, served piping hot and full of bold flavors. The chicken was tender, the vegetables were fresh, and the sauce complemented the dish perfectly. The sizzling presentation added to the excitement, and the portion size was quite satisfying.
A special mention goes to Shraddha from the staff, who made our experience even better. She was courteous, attentive, and very helpful with recommendations. Her service was prompt and professional, ensuring we were comfortable throughout the meal.
Overall, Wok Hei delivers a fantastic combination of delicious food, great ambiance, and excellent service. It’s a perfect spot for anyone craving quality Chinese food, and I would highly recommend it. Looking forward to visiting again and exploring more from their menu. 🍽️🔥

featured_reviews.review_text:
We had a special southindian lunch served by Jeevan Thali at our office in marol. The thali had absolutely amazing and truly satisfying. The meal was a perfect balance of flavors, textures, and authenticity. From the moment it was served, the aroma itself was enough to make me excited to dig in.

The thali included a variety of dishes like sambar, rasam, different vegetable curries, chutneys, all served with soft rice, crispy papad, and perfectly made chapatis, puranpoli, paysam. Each item had its own distinct taste—rich, flavorful, and well-seasoned without being too heavy.

What stood out the most was the freshness and authenticity of the preparation. The service was also warm and attentive, adding to the overall experience.

Overall, it was a wholesome, delicious, and fulfilling meal that truly represents the essence of South Indian cuisine. Definitely a must-try for anyone who loves traditional and flavorful food!

Highly recommend

featured_reviews.name: Gokulraj
featured_reviews.review_text:
Jeevan Boarding House in Chembur is a great spot if you're looking for delicious South Indian meals on a budget!

The ambiance is simple but pleasant, and the food is absolutely worth it.

It’s conveniently located—just a 1-minute walk from Chembur station—making it super easy to reach.

Their meals (Thali) are priced at just ₹90, which is a steal for the quality and quantity you get. Everything served beyond the basic meal is charged extra, but still very affordable.

Meals are served traditionally on a banana leaf, which adds to the authentic experience. The taste is amazing—especially their pineapple sweet and payasam, which are both top notch. You definitely won’t leave hungry, as the portions are more than enough!

Be prepared to wait if you visit during peak hoursit gets quite crowded after 1 PM, but the food is worth the wait. 😄

Highly recommended for anyone craving wholesome South Indian food!

featured_reviews.review_text:
I recently revisited Tayyabally’s Food Villa in Chembur, hoping the new, larger outlet would live up to the great food and service I’d experienced earlier at their smaller corner shop location. Instead, the visit was a complete disappointment, with food that was cold and stale and service that fell apart the moment I raised genuine concerns.

I ordered one Chicken Manchow soup, half Veg Fried Rice, half Chicken Hakka Noodles and Chicken Lollipop, but I was served an extra half Veg Hakka Noodles that I never asked for, and they refused to accept that it wasn’t ordered. The soup and lollipop were just about okay, but both the rice and noodles arrived barely warm and obviously not freshly prepared; when I pointed this out, the server’s only “solution” was to heat the same food in the oven for two minutes.

I was eventually allowed into the kitchen, where I saw exactly what I suspected: pre-made rice and noodles being used, and ready chicken lollipops simply reheated in oil before serving. I understand that some prep is done in advance for quick service, but if they are going to reheat, the least they can do is ensure the food is hot and not stale. Instead of acknowledging the quality issue and offering to make a fresh order, they tried to negotiate the bill down from ₹670 to ₹500, while I chose to pay the full amount and leave the food behind because I had serious concerns about freshness.

The restaurant is spacious but almost empty, which in hindsight should have been a clear warning about the standards here. The manager, who started off polite, became dismissive and rude once I raised these issues, and the serving staff appeared lethargic, uninterested and untrained, unwilling to listen or resolve anything properly.

Overall, my experience at the new Food Villa outlet in Chembur was of stale food, reheating shortcuts and unprofessional handling of feedback, and I have no intention of visiting again.

There are actually two Sindh Pani Puri Houses next to each other, but this one is the "original". You’ll know it by its modest, hand-painted sign (with the word “Original” on it) rather than flashy neon lights or LED boards of the adjacent one.

You’ll likely be greeted by a kind elderly gentleman who runs the stall. Seating is minimal—just a couple of stools by the kerb—so most people prefer to stand and enjoy their chaat right there. Prices are reasonable, and the taste is exactly what you’d hope for from a place that’s stayed true to its roots while others have modernized.

A charming, old-school spot that’s absolutely worth visiting at least once.
